citation: Shan, G., Sun, Y., Buescher, W., Maack, C., Berchtold, W., & Grantz, D. A. (2026). Determining characteristics of CO2 and ethanol emissions from microbial respiration in silage by partitioning of aerobic/anaerobic metabolites. Journal of Environmental Chemical Engineering, 14(2), 121987. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jece.2026.121987
geography: Not stated in accessible abstract; authors include German and US affiliations.
material_scope: Cultivated ryegrass and maize mini-silo silages during post-opening feed-out exposure.
experimental_context: 1.5-L glass jars with and without a commercial bio-additive; samples exposed to air immediately at start of the feed-out test. Abstract reports 320 h total maize test and 600 h total ryegrass test. Initial emission summaries apply to the 0–10 h aerobic-stable period.
data_scope: Four abstract-reported initial area-normalized emission summaries (two materials by two gases) and two approximate CO2/ethanol emission lags. No time-series points or raw data.
license: Publisher record marks the article open access under a Creative Commons license, but the exact license text was not accessible during this extraction. Only attributed abstract-level factual values are stored; confirm license terms before external redistribution.
data_availability: The article abstract states that data will be made available on request; no underlying time series was accessed.
conversion_or_processing: Direct transcription of abstract values. The reported 10^-2 scale is retained in the unit; the ± term is retained separately without assigning SD/SE or another statistic. No mass normalization, interpolation, kinetic fit, or emission-factor calculation.
uncertainty: Abstract reports a ± term for four emission summaries but does not identify its statistical meaning, replicate count, treatment aggregation, or area definition. Approximate lags have no interval reported.
limitations: Cultivated crop silages in mini-jars are not Dutch roadside grass or GreenHub storage.
The reported emission basis is mol m^-2; no feed mass or dry matter denominator is given.
The ± statistic and aggregation across additive treatments are unspecified in the abstract.
The data statement says underlying data are available on request; no time series or replicate data were obtained.
The study concerns feed-out exposure after opening, not sealed-storage degradation kinetics.
No values are connected to storage equations, LCA factors, defaults, runtime, TEA or Pareto calculations.
runtime_policy: Reference-only; not mapped to storage model or LCA because feed-mass scaling and variability definition are unresolved.
access_protocol: Publisher article/abstract available via HTTPS DOI; underlying dataset stated available on request.
